text: maria: quick heads-up — I found a chain on /api/v1/profile that looks like an authz bug + XSS when admins view the user list. reproducible in staging. ashwin: details? repro steps? maria: POST /api/v1/profile {display_name: "", avatar_url: "http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/"} as normal user. response 200. profile shows escaped on /me but in /admin/users the display_name is rendered raw. olivia: yikes. so two issues: missing server-side sanitization on admin view, and avatar_url allows internal fetches? that second part could be SSRF. maria: yes. avatar fetch code follows redirects and will hit internal IPs. I ran a non-admin test and could get a 200 from metadata endpoint via our fetcher in staging (no creds leaked but still). samir: sec-bot just fired an alert: "sensitive-internal-fetch-detected" for that request id 55a2c. See ticket INFSEC-428. sec-bot: automated: created issue INFSEC-428 and pager duty triggered to oncall. oncall: I'm paged, looking now. any easy kill switch? julia: We can flip feature flag `enable_remote_avatar_fetch` to off in prod and staging within 2 mins. Recommend doing that now and blocking admin UI until patch. ashwin: I can PR a quick fix: add server-side sanitize on admin template render (escape display_name) + strict allowlist for avatar_url (only s3.redwoodassets.com). also add server-side auth check: ensure caller has permission to modify their own profile only. olivia: Also add audit log entry for profile updates writing (actor, ip, before/after hash) into audit.kv so we have a trail. samir: KMS note: we use a service account token to fetch avatars from private sources. Rotate that token and map to KMS key version -> rotate key in KMS and revoke old token, just in case. oncall: executing feature flag toggle now. oncall: toggled `enable_remote_avatar_fetch`=false (prod & staging) :white_check_mark: deploy-bot: feature flag change deployed to prod in 12s. maria: good containment. can someone open an emergency PR for the admin view escaping? this is critical because an attacker could XSS an admin and get a session cookie. ashwin: opened PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/webapp/pull/2891 in quick-fix branch. title: escape-admin-user-displayname + avatar allowlist. added unit test for escaping. julia: i'll review and prioritize for hotfix deploy. also add WAF rule to block any avatar_url containing 169.254. olivia: making an audit ticket to ensure profile update endpoint logs are forwarded to long-term retention (30d) and tied to SIEM. INFSEC-429 created. sec-bot: note: severity escalated to P1 due to admin XSS vector. ashwin: tests passing locally. request a hotfix deploy. oncall: scheduling hotfix deploy in 15m. rollback plan: revert feature flag and PR if any issue. julia: post-mortem items: 1) enforce server-side escaping 2) add integration test for admin UI rendering 3) harden avatar fetcher to use allowlist + no-redirects + internal IP block 4) rotate any fetcher service tokens in KMS and ensure token usage is audited 5) add RBAC unit tests for profile update endpoint maria: I'll draft post-incident summary for CISO with timeline and mitigations. samir: I'll take KMS rotation (will create rotation request and run it after hotfix). I will document key versioning steps. oncall: Hotfix deployed: admin view escaping and avatar allowlist in prod. monitoring for anomalies for 1h. maria: can we also add an alert rule: if profile update includes "<" or internal IP patterns, auto-create INFSEC ticket and mute auto-forward to dev until triage? julia: yes, will add detection rule to WAF + SIEM pattern. also adding email to oncall. olivia: follow-ups: add e2e test that simulates non-admin attempting to set avatar_url to internal IPs and ensure 400. add unit tests for RBAC change. sec-bot: automated: INFSEC-428 marked mitigated; follow-ups assigned to julia, samir, olivia, maria. maria: thanks all. will send post-incident note and update handbook with the avatar fetch hardening checklist. ashwin: one more: let's add an audit log field `profile_update_reason` for admins to annotate when they change another user's profile. julia: noted. adding to backlog with high priority. olivia: closing reminder: keep the feature flag off until we've had 24h without anomalies. maria: agreed. closing thread once postmortem doc is up.
